derivation: Hand-transcribed rules of work/lead/cpl10-owner-preparation/lease-draft.md applied to the frozen financial pages with exact Fractions; cross-checked with decimal prec 38 ROUND_HALF_EVEN. No product code was imported or run by this builder; copied CP-1 cell classes were read from the real head by review probes (manifest.fact_selection_rule.observed).

cell_notation.shown: exact displayed text (report_view.fact_spelling); amounts decimals 2 (value cells MILLIONS, US$), percent 1 dp, multiple 2 dp, counts and rank 0 dp; a missing cell is `∅ G#` and a not_applicable cell is `∅ G# n.m.` (G# is the report-wide gap number bound at run time)
cell_notation.currency_scale: every fact with unit MILLIONS carries currency `USD` and scale `1000000` (CP-1's facts do); a MULTIPLE or PERCENT fact carries no currency and the default scale 1 (as CP-1's ratio facts)
cell_notation.calculation_id: a calculated own fact: `calc:<fact_id>`; a copied CP-1 cell: the marker `{{CP1_CALCULATION_ID}}`, the CP-1 fact's own canonical-kpi id bound at run time (every CP-1 T4.10 fact has one, source-class and missing ratio facts too); analyst and text-only cells: null
cell_notation.amount_exact: canonical exact decimal; null means unsettled
cell_notation.value_class_basis: observed on the real CP-1 head for every copied cell (manifest.fact_selection_rule); a missing ratio fact keeps value_class `calculated`
cell_notation.derives_from: the CP-1 T4.10 labels a calculated fact derives from
cell_notation.table_shape: every table of every case has one fact per column in every row, fact id <table>.<row>.<field> in column order (contracts.py:270-272, validate_tables); `tables[].columns` pins the order of the field names only; column labels are the product's and are not pinned; the builder asserts the shape for every table of both cases
cell_notation.not_applicable_text_cell: a text cell with no meaning for its row (the TL10.3 overall row's evidence, credit_transmission, screening_implication and source_refs): status not_applicable, shown `∅ G# n.m.`, limitation `Not applicable to the overall row`, no value class, no calculation id
cell_notation.run_bound_cells: TL10.1 scope_status and source_ref carry a marker, never a literal (manifest.run_time_bindings.tl10_1_scope_status, tl10_1_source_ref)

thresholds.basis: |closing - starting| / |starting| of CP-1 facts; screening-policy literals (D11) that no source states, stated in methods/cpl10.md with an own limitation, never presented as sourced
thresholds.exact_comparison: rated on the exact value, never on the rounded quotient or the shown percentage: Material iff abs(closing - starting) * 10 >= abs(starting); Watch iff abs(closing - starting) * 20 >= abs(starting); one rule for amounts and multiples; fixtures.composer pins the boundaries (99/2000 shows 5.0% yet is Stable)

rules.zero_base: starting value 0: change 0 -> Stable; change != 0 -> Material with change_pct not_applicable (never infinity, never 0)
rules.missing: either end missing -> change and change_pct missing (CP-1's limitation kept), materiality Not assessed, evidence Missing, disposition Evidence needed; never 0
rules.rank: Material, Watch, Not assessed, Stable; inside a class larger |change on starting level| first (zero-base Material first); then register order
rules.assessment_rule: exactly one analyst assessment for each topic Python rates Material or Watch; none for Stable or Not assessed

overall_rule.confidence_high: High is refused for every confidence, the overall's included (r07 pins the assessments[0] spelling `<path>.confidence: High is not allowed in a screen`)
overall_rule.insufficient_information_pairing: overall.confidence is Insufficient Information iff overall.category is Insufficient Information (r13; issue `overall.confidence: must be Insufficient Information exactly when the category is`)
overall_rule.limitation: an Insufficient Information overall (category) carries a non-null limitation (r14; `overall.limitation: an Insufficient Information overall states its limitation`); a category other than Insufficient Information forbids one (r15; `overall.limitation: only an Insufficient Information overall carries a limitation`); the CP-3C precedent, keyed on the category
overall_rule.issue_order: confidence High, then pairing, then limitation required, then limitation forbidden
overall_rule.literal_consequence: cases.limited.overall.limitation is null (it was a sentence on a Low-confidence Analyst Interpretation overall, which the forbidden-limitation rule now refuses)

gaps_rule.topic: each gap's `affected_analysis` equals a topic_id of the view or `overall` (r16; `gaps[<i>].affected_analysis: must name a topic of the view or overall`)
gaps_rule.missing_item: each gap's `gap` (the missing item) is non-empty after trimming (r17; `gaps[<i>].gap: empty`)
gaps_rule.no_digit: no gap text field (gap, why_it_matters, affected_analysis, action) contains a digit (r18; `gaps[<i>].<field>: must not contain a digit`)
gaps_rule.duplicates: a gap with the same `affected_analysis` and `gap` text as an earlier gap is refused (r19; `gaps[<i>]: repeated gap`)
gaps_rule.issue_order: per gap in order: topic, missing item, digit (field order gap, why_it_matters, affected_analysis, action), repeat
gaps_rule.literal_consequence: the positive gap's affected_analysis is `overall` (it was `Earnings and cash generation topics`, which the topic rule now refuses; r16 reuses that text)

rules.claim_citations: Claim.citations = the de-duplicated union, in first-reference order, of the citations of every fact the claim references, transitively through derives_from and the copied CP-1 cells (the CP-1C L3 rule: a calculated fact's citations are the ordered, de-duplicated concatenation of the citations of the facts in derives_from; a copied cell carries its CP-1 fact's citations). A claim that references no fact carries none
rules.lineage_citations: a calculated own fact's citations follow the same rule over its derives_from (the CP-1C L3 rule); a count fact has no derives_from, and a missing change or change_pct cell has none either, so a claim that references only counts or only a missing change carries no citations as the facts stand (a derives_from on those cells would be a fact-value change outside amendment 1)

submission_types.note: the field types decide shape versus content; pinned here, frozen with the lease
submission_types.assessments[].topic_id, assessment, cred: Text (contracts.Text); whitespace-only text passes the type and is a content refusal
submission_types.confidence: business_context.Confidence (admits High: High is a content refusal, as CP-2A)
submission_types.shape issues: missing field, wrong type, empty string (min_length): `<dotted.path>: <pydantic message>`, returned alone

validation_order: comparison (an issue here ENDS validation: the ratings depend on the pair)
assessments[] in submission order, then the missing-assessment check

analyst text of every assessment and overall: bare figures and references through the product prose path against the module's bound facts (fact ids and unique calculation ids), prohibited conclusions, empty text

own_limitations: Relative-change thresholds are screening rules documented in the CP-L10 method; they are not covenant or credit tests.
Only the two quarters named in the comparison are compared; no trend, seasonality or annual comparison is made, and the pack has no prior-year statements.
Leverage and coverage are compared only where CP-1 carries a twelve-month basis for both quarters.
A screen rates movement, not credit quality: no recommendation, covenant, recovery or refinancing conclusion is drawn.
Each topic is rated on the exact change on its starting level; the percentage shown is rounded, so a shown value at a threshold can carry the lower rating.
A small starting level inflates the relative change and a negative starting level is measured on its absolute value, so the rating reads the size of movement, not its economic meaning.

own_limitations: Relative-change thresholds are screening rules documented in the CP-L10 method; they are not covenant or credit tests.
Only the two quarters named in the comparison are compared; no trend, seasonality or annual comparison is made, and the pack has no prior-year statements.
Leverage and coverage are compared only where CP-1 carries a twelve-month basis for both quarters.
A screen rates movement, not credit quality: no recommendation, covenant, recovery or refinancing conclusion is drawn.
Each topic is rated on the exact change on its starting level; the percentage shown is rounded, so a shown value at a threshold can carry the lower rating.
A small starting level inflates the relative change and a negative starting level is measured on its absolute value, so the rating reads the size of movement, not its economic meaning.
